# EfficientViT (MIT)

**Category:** Efficient/Mobile · **Code:**
[`timm/models/efficientvit_mit.py`](https://github.com/huggingface/pytorch-image-models/blob/main/timm/models/efficientvit_mit.py)
· **Architectures:** 7 · **Pretrained weights:** 19 (19 with ImageNet-1k results)

EfficientViT from the MIT Han Lab, a vision backbone for high-resolution, low-computation recognition that uses
multi-scale linear attention.

## Papers

* [EfficientViT: Multi-Scale Linear Attention for High-Resolution Dense Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14756)

## Usage

See the [Quickstart](../quickstart) for loading pretrained weights, image preprocessing and fine-tuning, and [Feature
Extraction](../feature_extraction) for using the models as backbones.

```py
>>> import timm
>>> model = timm.create_model('efficientvit_b2.r224_in1k', pretrained=True)
>>> data_config = timm.data.resolve_model_data_config(model)
```

## Model API support

| Feature | `EfficientVit` | `EfficientVitLarge` |
|---|---|---|
| [`features_only=True` feature maps](../model_api#intermediate-features) | ✓ (strides 4, 8, 16, 32) | ✓ (strides 4, 8, 16, 32) |
| [`forward_intermediates()`](../model_api#intermediate-features) | ✓ | ✓ |
| [`prune_intermediate_layers()`](../model_api#intermediate-features) | ✓ | ✓ |
| [Any input size, no changes needed](../model_api#input-size) | ✓ | ✓ |
| [`set_input_size()`](../model_api#input-size) | – | – |
| [`dynamic_img_size=True`](../model_api#input-size) | – | – |
| [`set_grad_checkpointing()`](../model_api#training-hooks) | ✓ | ✓ |
| [Layer-wise LR decay (`group_matcher()`)](../model_api#training-hooks) | ✓ | ✓ |
| [`reset_classifier()`](../model_api#classifier) | ✓ | ✓ |

✓ supported, ✓ (square) works for square sizes only, ✗ not supported, – not needed (the model already accepts any input
size). Checked by running each feature on a randomly initialized model (`EfficientVit` with `efficientvit_b0` at 224,
`EfficientVitLarge` with `efficientvit_l1` at 224), other architectures of the same class are expected to behave the
same. See the [Model API](../model_api) page for details.
